title: DSX shot properties
description: The machine-readable property schema for STORE SCREENSHOT slides: every editable field of a shot profile, typed and constrained, so a visual editor renders real controls instead of a JSON textarea. This is the shot plane's twin of stack-style-properties.json, and it is a CONTRACT rather than documentation: check_shot_properties.rb fails when the templates read a field the schema does not describe, or the schema offers a control the templates never read.

source.profiles: dsx.shots.json (the project's shot profiles - what an editor writes)

controlTypes.length: CSS length string - the unit is part of the value. A control whose `units` lists more than one may be switched between them, and switching CONVERTS the number rather than reinterpreting it (16px is 1rem, never 16rem): a switch that silently made a headline sixteen times larger would be a unit picker nobody could trust. rem is the default the editor writes for a bare number, because rem is root-relative and the root is accessibility-scaled.
controlTypes.parts: the two-tone headline array: [{t, accent?, box?}]
controlTypes.region: a {x,y,w,h} rectangle in percent of the source screenshot

groups.label: Theme
groups.help: Set once for the whole strip: shared values are most of what makes a set read as designed.

properties.label: Page
properties.help: The neutral behind the slide. Only visible with a gutter, since a full-bleed slide covers it.

properties.label: Card
properties.help: The slide surface, edge to edge at gutter 0. The dissolve fades into this exact colour.

properties.label: Ink
properties.help: Headline and copy colour.

properties.label: Accent
properties.help: The emphasis colour for headline parts, rings and panels.

properties.label: Headline
properties.help: Two-tone headline. Each part: t (text), accent (accent ink) or box (filled highlight).

properties.label: Gutter
properties.help: Margin around the whole slide. 0 is full bleed, which is what a store uploads; a gutter turns the slide into an inset card on the page colour.

properties.label: Corner
properties.help: Corner radius of the slide. Only visible with a gutter, since a full-bleed image has no corner to round.

properties.label: Tagline
properties.help: One line of support under the headline.

properties.label: Measure
properties.help: Line length in em, so it holds characters-per-line and rebalances when the size changes. This is what kills a one-word last line.

properties.label: Screen
properties.help: The captured app screenshot this slide shows.

properties.label: Width
properties.help: Percent of the SAFE width. 100% is the largest lawful phone - the safe inset is structural.

properties.label: Crop
properties.help: Empty shows the whole device. Set it and the phone runs past the edge and dissolves.

properties.label: Dissolve
properties.help: The progressive blur at the crop edge.

properties.label: Lean
properties.help: Turn the device about its own Y axis, with real foreshortening.

properties.label: Specular
properties.help: One raking highlight across the cover glass.

properties.label: Safe inset
properties.help: The breathing room the card keeps around its content. G-safe enforces it on the rendered frame.

groups.label: Feature chips
groups.help: Flow content: chips reserve their own band, so they can never land on the app screen.

placement.label: Placement
placement.help: Every decoration carries these. x/y/w/h are percentages of the card, so a decoration means the same thing at every device size.

properties.label: Lean
properties.help: Share the device's camera. A flat card beside a turned phone is the tell that reads as collage.

properties.label: Anchor
properties.help: card: the decoration is placed on the slide. device: it rides the phone and the crop clips it with it.

properties.label: Over UI
properties.help: Covering readable app UI is legal only when declared. Undeclared, the render REFUSES (G-cover).

properties.label: Bleed
properties.help: Running off the card edge is legal only when declared, or the render refuses (G-safe).

decorKinds.label: Image
decorKinds.help: The customer's own artwork - a logo, a mascot, a product shot.

decorKinds.label: Rating badge
decorKinds.help: A claim the customer can substantiate. There is no store-award badge here, on purpose.

decorKinds.label: Laurel
decorKinds.help: A generic decorative wreath: it carries no store mark, no Play laurel, no App Store wording.

decorKinds.label: Arrow
decorKinds.help: A ring says look here; an arrow says look here, from over there.

decorKinds.label: Panel
decorKinds.help: An accent-tinted block behind supporting copy.

decorKinds.label: Callout ring
decorKinds.help: The ring has NO fill: annotation must never obscure the UI it points at.

decorKinds.label: Zoom
decorKinds.help: A magnified crop of the SAME render the device shows - real UI at real fidelity, never a mock.
